data.title: Norfolk Southern/Union Pacific deal spread widens amid report on UNP CEO's remarks
data.description:
The deal spread in Union Pacific's (UNP) planned $72 billion purchase of competitor Norfolk Southern (NSC) widened amid a report highlighting some remarks that the UNP CEO made earlier this year. The spread widened to $63 from $60 on Thursday.

Union Pacific (UNP) CEO made a remark at an industry event in March, basically threatening anyone who spoke out against the mega rail deal, the WSJ highlighted in a report on Friday.

"I'll probably increase everybody's rates that said they didn't want a seamless railroad by three or four extra percent to teach you a lesson," Vena said in a video recording of his remarks.

Union Pacific (UNP) spent months to keep the video from being released, according to the report. Now that it's public, farmers, chemical makers, and other opponents have amped up their concerns about a railroad combination.

The Surface Transportation Board, the regulator that will rule on the deal, ordered Union Pacific (UNP) to release the video of Vena's remarks and added that it has “serious concerns” that the CEO's comments may impact the willingness of those who may be impacted by the transaction to express their view, the WSJ said. 

Union Pacific (UNP) said it doesn't retaliate against customers and that its CEO made an offhand remark. "Vena is known for being a dynamic speaker," the railroad said.

Some traders on Friday also told Seeking Alpha the deal spread may have increased due to speculation that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who appeared to be a champion of the railroad deal, could lose his job as White House senior officials are reportedly discussing whether he should keep his role after a spy scandal surrounding Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang.

There was a report on Monday that the Dept. of Justice is expected to give its opinion on the deal by Dec. 3. The DOJ is likely to remain neutral on the rail combination, according to traders, who cited a Capitol Forum report.

data.title: Go Residential sues H&R REIT after shareholders reject acquisition offer
data.description:
Go Residential REIT (GO.U:CA) (GO.U) has sued H&R Real Estate Investment Trust (HR.UN:CA) (HRUFF) after the latter's investors rejected an acquisition offer by Blackstone (BX), Go, and other buyers.

The offer would have split H&R's properties among several buyers, with Go set to acquire the U.S. apartment portfolio and Blackstone and other investors, including Canada's Public Sector Pension Investment Board, getting industrial properties, Bloomberg News reported on Friday.

Additionally, H&R CEO Tom Hofstedter-affiliated company CRAL would have taken over some office buildings, development sites, land, and other assets, according to the report.

The unusual arrangement reportedly sparked a revolt among major investors.

Go Residential filed proceedings against H&R and others in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, seeking a termination fee of C$102.13M and other relief arising from alleged breaches of the August arrangement agreement.

In the claim, Go Residential alleges that H&R REIT failed to comply with its contractual obligations and duty of good faith and honest performance under the arrangement agreement. The REIT allegedly failed to maintain its support for the transaction and undermined its board's prior unanimous, unqualified recommendation in favor of the transaction.

data.title: West Coast Community approves $25M share buyback program; shares surge
data.description:
• West Coast Community (WCCB) announced on Friday that its board approved a $25M share repurchase program.

  • The company may repurchase shares through open-market purchases or privately negotiated transactions, subject to market conditions.

  • The program runs through December 31, 2028, but does not require the company to buy any specific number of shares.

  • The repurchases will be funded through internal cash resources, supplemented if needed by dividends from West Coast Community Bank.

  • CEO Krista Snelling said the program reflects confidence in the company's balance sheet and long-term value while maintaining flexibility for future investments.

  • The stock surged 3% to $65.41 in the after-hours session, while the program remains subject to customary regulatory approvals or non-objections.
